Short answers to common questions. The button under an answer opens the setting it is about.
How do I make Ogneliss Dialer my default phone app?

On first launch the app offers to become the default phone app. If you declined, open %1$s and choose Ogneliss Dialer under “Phone” — the name varies slightly between phones. Your call log and contacts stay as they are: Android keeps them, not the app, so nothing is lost if you switch back. If the app was installed from an APK file and Android says “Restricted setting”, open App info → ⋮ → “Allow restricted settings” first.
Why doesn’t the app have internet access?

So that your data cannot leave the phone. Without the internet permission the app cannot send anything — not the call log, not contacts, not notes; you can see this in the installed app details. The operator and region of an unknown number come from a directory inside the app, and whether to show them is up to you: %1$s.
How do I move notes and lists to a new phone?

With a file. They won’t move by themselves: the app keeps its data out of cloud backups and phone-to-phone transfers, so it stays with you only. Open %1$s — your notes, tags, block and allow lists and speed dial are saved to a file you choose. On the new phone use %2$s: the data is added to what is already there. The call log and contacts are moved by Android and your account.
How do I switch from the call log to contacts?

With the first button on the bottom bar. The large icon is the list that is open now; the small circle next to it is where a tap takes you. A long press opens all sections: call log, contacts, notes and reminders. You can also swipe along the bar: left for contacts, right to go back to the call log.
How do I find a contact by name?

With the “Search” button on the bottom bar. In the call log it searches names, numbers and notes; in contacts, names. The dial pad searches with digits too — by number and by T9, in Cyrillic and Latin at once.
I deleted a call log entry by mistake. Can I get it back?

Yes, if you act right away. After deleting, “Removed from the call list” with an “Undo” button appears at the bottom for a few seconds — tap it while the message is shown. After that the entries are removed from the phone’s system call log too and cannot be restored. Clearing the whole call log from the menu cannot be undone, which is why the app asks first.
How do I block spam and unwanted numbers?

Long-press an entry → “Block”: the number goes to the block list and can no longer get through. In the same place, under “More”, there is the “Spam” tag: such numbers can’t get through either, and the tag is shown in the call log and on the call screen. Number masks, hidden and unknown numbers and an allow list of exceptions are in %1$s.
How do I answer calls by sliding — or get the buttons back?

%1$s. “Tap” gives two ordinary buttons. With “Slide” you move the button: right to answer, left to decline — so a call is not answered or rejected by accident while you take the phone out of your pocket. With TalkBack, calls are always answered with buttons.
How do I choose the SIM card for a call?

Long-press any call or SMS button — in the call log, contacts, a contact card — and choose the card for that action. The app remembers the card chosen for a number and offers it again next time (%1$s). To tell the cards apart, name them: %2$s.
Missed calls only appear when I open the app. What can I do?
Most likely the system puts the app to sleep to save battery. Allow it to work in the background — %1$s — and missed calls will appear right away.
The call screen does not appear for incoming calls. What can I do?

Some phones — Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO, vivo, OPPO, realme, OnePlus — do not let apps show windows over the lock screen or from the background by default. Open %1$s and allow showing on the lock screen and pop-up windows in the background. On Huawei, Honor, Tecno and Infinix also allow auto-start. Until then you can answer from the call notification.

No. On Android 10 and later the system gives third-party apps no access to call audio, and working around this breaks Google Play rules. If your phone records calls, that is a feature built in by the manufacturer — it works regardless of the dialer you use.
Can I use the app at work? Where is the source code?

Yes. The app’s code is open under the Apache License 2.0: you may use it for any lawful purpose, including work and business. You may also share the APK and your own versions — together with the license text and the NOTICE file; the name and icon stay with the original. The source code is on GitHub.
How do I report a bug or suggest an idea?
Write to oedante@gmail.com. If something doesn’t work right, attach the technical log — %1$s: numbers and names in it are masked.

How do I get through when the line is busy?

After “Busy” or “No answer”, the call screen offers “Keep trying”: the app dials the number again after a pause, as many times as set (%2$s). To redial without asking, choose “Right away” in %1$s. Emergency and short service numbers are never redialed, and “End call” always stops it.
Can I avoid hearing night calls from unknown numbers?

Yes: %1$s. During those hours such a call comes in silently and doesn’t wake the screen; in the morning it’s in the call log marked “Silenced — quiet hours”. If the same number calls again within 15 minutes, the phone rings. Contacts and numbers on the allow list always ring.
Why does a number show a company name “from your carrier”?

Many organizations call with a label: the carrier sends the company name along with the number (in Russia this is required since 1 September 2025). The app shows it on the call screen and keeps it for the call log and the contact card — for numbers not in your contacts. The name comes from the network, not from the app: your contacts and notes always take priority.
What is the fraud reminder during a call?

If a call with an unknown number lasts over two minutes, the call screen reminds you once: never share SMS codes, card details or passwords. The app doesn’t listen to the call and doesn’t know who’s on the line — the rule holds for any call. Turn it off here: %1$s.

Can I send and receive SMS in the dialer?

Yes, if you choose to. Sending: the “Message” buttons open the conversation right here (%1$s) — the dialer must be your default phone app for that. Receiving, the conversation history and pictures (MMS) need the dialer to be your default SMS app (%2$s). Then messages appear in the call log alongside calls, and the call log filter can show only calls or only messages. To stop, choose another SMS app at any time — the dialer stops reading messages right away. RCS chat is not available to third-party apps.
How do I paste a code from an SMS?

When a message contains a verification code, the notification gets a “Copy 123456” button, and the conversation shows the same button under the message. The code goes to the clipboard marked as sensitive, and your keyboard offers to paste it with one tap. Filling the code into another app automatically is done by your keyboard or autofill service (for example, Gboard or Autofill with Google) — that keeps working with the dialer as your SMS app. The code is found on the phone: the dialer has no internet access. Long-press a message to copy the whole text, a phone number from it, or select any part.
